extracted.intended_audience: research authors, reviewers, and editors in the life sciences and medicine considering or participating in eLife's Reviewed Preprint publishing model
extracted.subtask_description: Describes eLife's Reviewed Preprint publishing model and the principles, outputs, and procedural rules that govern which preprints are reviewed, how peer review is conducted and published, fees, and options for Version of Record publication. Aimed at people submitting or participating in peer review at eLife.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprint-only review policy
rubrics_metrics.description: We only review articles that have been made available as preprints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: eLife's model requires availability as a preprint to combine immediacy/openness with peer review scrutiny; submissions not posted as preprints are not eligible for this review route.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editor eligibility and selection role
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors who are active researchers decide which preprints are reviewed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection of preprints for review is made by practising researchers (editors) to ensure decisions are informed by current domain expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative discussion between editors and reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors and reviewers discuss the reviews with each other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer review involves dialogue among editorial staff and reviewers to refine assessments and ensure clarity and consistency before publication of reviews and assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: No accept/reject decision after peer review for Reviewed Preprints
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no accept/reject decision after peer review: rather, every article we review is published on the eLife website as a Reviewed Preprint that includes an eLife assessment, public reviews, and a response from the authors (if available).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The outcome of review is public assessment and reviews rather than a binary editorial decision; authors retain control to seek Version of Record publication later if they choose.

rubrics_metrics.name: No artificial limit on number reviewed or published
rubrics_metrics.description: We do not artificially limit the number of articles we review or publish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: eLife does not impose quotas on reviewed preprints; selection is based on editorial judgment rather than fixed publication caps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Option to convert Reviewed Preprint to Version of Record
rubrics_metrics.description: At any point following peer review, authors can choose to have their Reviewed Preprint published as a regular journal article. This version (known as the Version of Record) will be sent to indexers including PubMed, Scopus and Web of Science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors can opt into traditional journal publishing after the Reviewed Preprint stage to obtain indexing and formal Version of Record metadata.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishing fee and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The fee for publishing an article with eLife is $2,000, charged at the point we commit to peer reviewing the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The processing/publication fee is payable when eLife commits to carrying out peer review (i.e., before completion of review); authors and funders should plan for this cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with funder open-access requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Publication of an eLife Version of Record complies with all major funding agency requirements for immediate online access to the published results of their research grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: eLife's Version of Record meets funder mandates for immediate open access, and funders are increasingly recognising Reviewed Preprints in assessment contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: eLife assessment: content and authorship
rubrics_metrics.description: An eLife assessment that summarises the significance of the findings and the strength of the evidence; the editor and the reviewers write this assessment with the help of a common vocabulary to ensure consistency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessments are concise summaries prepared collaboratively by editor(s) and reviewers, using standardised language to communicate both importance and evidentiary strength to readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public reviews: scope and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Public reviews that describe the strengths and weaknesses of the article, and indicate whether the claims and conclusions are justified by the data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews are published openly to document detailed reviewer evaluations, focusing on which aspects are well supported and which are not, so readers can judge the validity of claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendations for authors produced but not published with Reviewed Preprints
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendations for the authors, including suggestions for revising and improving the article. These recommendations are not included in the Reviewed Preprint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While reviewers provide actionable revision suggestions to authors, these specific recommendations are excluded from the public Reviewed Preprint package (which contains assessment, reviews, and author response).

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of traditional review model (temporary)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a limited period authors can ask for submissions to be reviewed under eLife’s traditional model (which includes an accept/reject decision after peer review).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may temporarily opt into the conventional accept/reject editorial decision process rather than the Reviewed Preprint route; this option is time-limited.
